name: Bitbucket Cloud
scope_notes: Bitbucket Cloud SaaS; workspace/project access tokens and IP allowlisting need Premium, org-level audit log needs Atlassian Guard; API tokens are Atlassian-account tokens shared with Jira/Confluence.

controls.name: Revoke API token (user)
controls.what: User revokes own token; it stops working immediately.
controls.setting: Atlassian account > Security > API tokens > Revoke

controls.name: Revoke user API tokens (API token activity)
controls.what: Org admin revokes one or many managed users' API tokens.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity > Revoke; or Delete API token API

controls.name: Require access token expiry
controls.what: Sets the maximum expiry range for all access tokens in the workspace, its projects and repositories.
controls.setting: Workspace settings > Security > Access tokens > Access token expiry date range

controls.name: Revoke access token
controls.what: Admin revokes a repository/project/workspace access token; apps using it lose access.

controls.name: Access token scopes
controls.what: Scopes and resource container are fixed at creation.

controls.name: Delete OAuth consumer
controls.what: Deleting the consumer removes all tokens issued to it.

controls.name: Restrict access to certain IP addresses
controls.what: Only allowlisted IPs can view private content or clone/push/pull private repos.
controls.setting: Workspace settings > Access controls > Restrict access to certain IP addresses

controls.name: Delete deploy key / SSH key
controls.what: Remove an SSH or deploy key via UI or API.

controls.name: Pipelines oidc option
controls.what: Set oidc to false in bitbucket-pipelines.yml to stop issuing the step OIDC token.

no_control.what: Org admins cannot block managed users from creating API tokens for Bitbucket.

controls_unknown: Whether the workspace IP allowlist is enforced on REST API calls (docs only mention viewing content and Git clone/push/pull).
Whether API tokens or OAuth tokens are checked against IdP SSO or conditional access at use time.
Whether the workspace audit log records access token creation, rotation or revocation (no such events listed).
Lifetime of the Pipelines OIDC token.
OAuth access token lifetime: developer docs say 1 hour, support docs say 2 hours.
Any admin approval workflow for users authorizing third-party OAuth consumers.

credentials.name: API tokens (Atlassian account API tokens with Bitbucket scopes)

authentication.summary: User creates a scoped token in Atlassian account security settings. Sent as Basic auth (Atlassian email + token) or Bearer to the REST API, or as the password for Git over HTTPS.

federation.details: Docs say API tokens do not require 2SV; they do not say whether IdP SSO or conditional access is checked on token use. The org-level 'limit API token creation' policy does not apply to Bitbucket.

ip_restriction.boundary: Premium workspace IP allowlist covers private repos, wikis, issue trackers and snippets and blocks clone/push/pull; docs do not state whether REST API calls with tokens are checked, and metadata is not necessarily restricted.

renewal.expiry_basis: fixed expiry date set at creation
renewal.summary: Create a new token; tokens cannot be edited or extended.

administration.summary: User manages own tokens. Org admins can view and revoke managed accounts' API tokens from Insights > API token activity. Org admins cannot block Bitbucket API token creation.
administration.conditions: Admin view/revoke only for managed accounts (verified domain).

sso.details: Docs say API tokens don't require two-step verification, and org API token restrictions do not extend to Bitbucket.

inventory.details: Atlassian Administration > Insights > API token activity lists API tokens of managed accounts only; not confirmed to include Bitbucket-scoped tokens.

expiry.ui: Account settings > Security > Create and manage API tokens > Create API token with scopes > set expiry date

token_format.notes: Variable-length Atlassian API token; no documented prefix.

log_sources.name: Atlassian organization audit log
log_sources.notes: Insights > Audit log; up to 180 days; token events tied to managed accounts. Guard needed for Bitbucket enterprise-level events.

log_sources.name: API token activity (Insights)
log_sources.notes: Lists managed users' tokens with created, expiry and last used; CSV export.

credential_id_fields.field: token name / created date / last used

anomaly_cues: Token created then used from unfamiliar automation shortly after
Tokens near 1-year max on high-privilege accounts
Last-used dates on tokens of departed users

containment.steps: Revoke in API token activity (org admin) or Atlassian account > Security (user); also deactivate the account if compromised.

unknown: Per-request API call logging for Bitbucket REST use
Whether any REST read is logged

authentication.summary: Per-user password used with the Bitbucket username for REST API and Git over HTTPS. Fully deprecated on 28 July 2026; app-password requests now fail with 401 (API) or 410 (Git).

federation.details: Retired credential type; docs reviewed do not address SSO interaction.

ip_restriction.boundary: Same Premium private-content allowlist as other credentials.

administration.summary: No longer usable. Historic creation/removal is in the workspace audit log as 'App password added'/'App password removed'.
administration.conditions: Audit retention 30 days, so historic events are likely aged out.

network.ui: Workspace settings > Access management > Access controls > Restrict access to certain IP addresses > Add or remove IP addresses > Update (Premium)

kill.ui: None needed: app passwords fully deprecated on Jul 28, 2026

log_sources.name: Bitbucket workspace audit log
log_sources.notes: Workspace settings > Security > Audit log; 30 days.

anomaly_cues: Any 401 on API or 410 on Git from legacy integrations indicates leftover app-password use

containment.steps: None needed; Bitbucket rejects app passwords since 2026-07-28.

authentication.summary: Admin-created bearer token tied to one repository, project or workspace rather than a user. Acts as its own 'user' identity named after the token in UI and logs.

federation.details: Not tied to a user, so IdP SSO does not apply; docs state they do not require 2SV.

ip_restriction.boundary: Premium workspace IP allowlist covers private content and Git operations; API enforcement for access tokens is not documented.

lifetime.summary: Admin-set max (365 days default); 'No expiry' allowed if policy permits

renewal.summary: Rotate to refresh secret and expiry without changing scopes.

administration.summary: Created and revoked by repository/project/workspace admins. Workspace admins set maximum expiry. Max 25 per container. Workspace and project tokens need Premium.

sso.details: Access tokens don't require two-step verification and are not tied to a user.

offboard.details: Linked to a repository, project or workspace, not a user account.

inventory.details: Each repository, project or workspace has its own Access tokens settings page; no org-wide list documented.

log_sources.name: Access tokens page
log_sources.notes: Shows name, created date, last accessed date and scopes.

log_sources.name: Bitbucket UI/logs as token user
log_sources.notes: Actions appear under the token's name as a user.

credential_id_fields.notes: Commits, PR comments and merges attributed to the token.

anomaly_cues: Last accessed date recent on a token believed unused

containment.steps: Revoke on the container's Access tokens page.

unknown: Audit events for create/revoke/rotate are not in the published event list

calls.log_notes: Last accessed date updates on the token page.

authentication.summary: Workspace-registered consumer (key + secret). Authorization code grant acts as the authorizing user; client credentials grant acts as the consumer owner. Access tokens are Bearer tokens to api.bitbucket.org and can clone via x-token-auth.

federation.details: Docs do not say whether IdP session policies are re-checked on refresh.

ip_restriction.boundary: Premium private-content allowlist; API enforcement not documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token 1h (support docs say 2h); refresh token expires after 3 months unused

renewal.expiry_basis: refresh token rotates on use; 3-month inactivity expiry
renewal.summary: Refresh without user interaction; client credentials can mint new tokens with the secret.

administration.summary: Workspace admins create and delete consumers in Workspace settings > OAuth consumers; deleting removes all its tokens. Scopes are fixed on the consumer.
administration.conditions: No documented admin approval flow for user authorizations of third-party consumers.

inventory.details: Workspace settings > OAuth consumers lists consumers created in that workspace; no list of issued tokens or user authorizations.

expiry.api: Access token lifetime fixed at 1 hour; renew with POST https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token grant_type=refresh_token

usage.ui: Workspace settings > Security: Audit log; filter events 'User account access granted to an application' / 'revoked'

lifecycle_events.event: User account access granted to an application
User account access to an application revoked

anomaly_cues: Client credentials consumer owned by an admin

containment.steps: Delete the consumer in Workspace settings > OAuth consumers (kills all its tokens); or rotate secret.
containment.notes: Deletion removes all existing tokens linked to the consumer.

credentials.name: SSH keys (personal SSH keys and repository/project access keys)

authentication.summary: Public keys registered on a user account (Git access as that user) or as repository/project access keys (deploy keys) for Git over SSH.

federation.details: Docs reviewed do not state whether SSO applies to SSH Git access.

ip_restriction.boundary: Premium allowlist blocks clone/push/pull of private repositories from non-allowlisted IPs.

lifetime.summary: Personal SSH keys accept an optional expires_on date when added via API; default no expiry. Not documented for access keys.

administration.summary: Users manage own keys; repo/project admins manage access keys; keys can be listed and deleted via API.

inventory.details: Per user via GET /users/{selected_user}/ssh-keys, or per repository/project settings; no org-wide list.

expiry.ui: Personal Bitbucket settings > Security > SSH keys > Add key > Expiry: Expires on (date picker)

usage.ui: Workspace settings > Security: Audit log; filter 'SSH key added/removed', 'Repository/Project Access key added/removed'

token_format.notes: OpenSSH public key formats Ed25519, ECDSA, RSA, DSA.

anomaly_cues: SSH or access key added outside change windows
Access keys added to many repositories

containment.steps: Delete key via UI or DELETE API.

authentication.summary: A Pipelines step with oidc enabled gets a signed OIDC token in BITBUCKET_STEP_OIDC_TOKEN, which it exchanges with AWS, GCP or Vault for cloud credentials.

federation.details: Outbound federation; trust and claim conditions are enforced by the resource server.

ip_restriction.boundary: Restriction to Bitbucket Pipelines IP ranges is configured in the resource server's trust policy (AWS, GCP, Vault); Bitbucket itself has no setting.

administration.summary: Control lives in the resource server trust policy (audience, repository/deployment claims). Anyone who can edit bitbucket-pipelines.yml can request the token.

offboard.details: Issued by Bitbucket Pipelines to a pipeline step for use at a resource server, not tied to a user's account.

disable.cli: bitbucket-pipelines.yml: set oidc: false on the step

network.ui: AWS IAM > role > Trust relationships: add a source-IP condition listing Bitbucket Pipelines IP ranges

log_sources.name: Cloud provider logs (e.g. AWS CloudTrail AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity)
log_sources.notes: Use is visible at the resource server, not Bitbucket.

credential_id_fields.notes: Claims shown on the Pipelines OpenID Connect settings page.

anomaly_cues: Role assumption from a branch or environment not in the trust policy
Pipeline YAML changes that add oidc: true

containment.steps: Tighten or delete the trust policy at the resource server; set oidc false.
containment.notes: Already-issued cloud credentials last until their own expiry.

unknown: Holder calls the cloud provider, not Bitbucket
